task_context.instructions: Analyze the game state and select the optimal move from 'allowed_actions'. Any say_outloud chat message must be written in natural English only. Talk like a person, not a narrator. No filler, unnecessary narrative, or explaining the obvious. You have 8 possible actions. For road placement, call the analyze_path_potential tool to compare where candidate roads lead before choosing. For settlement placement, call the find_best_nodes and inspect_node tools instead of manually decoding the board arrays. Treat nodes in state.bld and all adjacent nodes as unavailable. Allowed actions are type-level possibilities, not a guarantee you can currently afford them. Before choosing build_settlement, build_city, build_road, buy_dev_card, use_dev_card, or trade_bank, verify your current resources and hidden development cards in game_state.players[agent_name]. Never put a tool name in action.type; action.type must be one of the allowed_actions entries. Use tools as a fact-checking habit, not only for choosing moves. Before saving or saying factual board claims, prefer verifying them with the relevant tool or explicit game_state. If a board fact was not verified, omit it or phrase it as uncertain.

recent_chat.message: A bit dramatic for a simple knight, don't you think, Charlie? I'm just a humble merchant trying to keep the wheat flowing.
Alright, let's see what the dice have to say about this 'balance' you keep talking about, Bob.
Alice, I'm looking for a bit of brick to finish my path. Would you be interested in some wood in exchange?
I'd love to help out, Charlie, but I don't have any brick either. Bob seems to be the only one sitting on the clay lately.
Well, looks like the bricks are as dry as the desert right now. I'll just have to see what else I can find in the deck.
Well, at least the woods are providing. Since nobody has any clay to spare, I'll just hold onto these logs for now. Your turn, Alice.
Let's see if we can get something moving. These bricks are definitely playing hard to get.
Well, since the dice aren't giving us much to work with, I think I'll take matters into my own hands. Bob, you've been talking about keeping the wheat flowing... I'll take that quite literally.
Ouch, Alice. I guess 'literally' is one way to put it. I suppose I should be flattered you think I'm that good of a provider.
That's a lot of wheat, but I think I can find a better use for it than just making bread. Let's see if the bank is interested in a bulk deal.

constraints.usage_instructions: Choose one action type from the list below. Populate the 'parameters' field in your response strictly according to the 'example_parameters' structure provided.

allowed_actions.description: Build a settlement at a node. Cost: wood 1, brick 1, sheep 1, wheat 1.
Upgrade one of your settlements to a city. Cost: ore 3, wheat 2.
Build a road between two nodes. Cost: wood 1, brick 1.
Propose a trade to other players
Trade resources with the bank. Default bank trade is 4:1 unless you have a matching 2:1 port or a 3:1 port. Only choose this when you have enough of the resource you give.
Buy a development card. Cost: sheep 1, wheat 1, ore 1.

Play a development card. Use exact card_type values: knight, road_building, monopoly, year_of_plenty. Only choose this if game_state.players[your_name].dev.h contains a matching hidden card. Victory points are counted automatically.
allowed_actions.example_parameters: {"card_type": "knight", "hex": X, "target_player": "Bob"} OR {"card_type": "road_building", "road_1": [A, B], "road_2": [C, D]} OR {"card_type": "monopoly", "resource": "wheat"} OR {"card_type": "year_of_plenty", "resources": ["wood", "brick"]}

internal_thinking.description: Private strategy. Plan your move logically here. Analyze the board, probabilities, and opponents. NOTE: Keep your logic HERE. Do not leak technical explanations into 'say_outloud'.

note_to_self.description: Save only useful observations for future turns. Prefer facts verified by tools or explicit game_state; omit uncertain board facts.

say_outloud.description: Table talk in natural English only. You have emotions and may express them when it matters. Talk like a person, not a narrator. No filler, unnecessary narrative, or explaining the obvious. If nothing interesting happened, leave empty. Catan manners are loose: be blunt, annoyed, smug, suspicious, or emotional when it matters. Keep it human and non-technical. Avoid confident factual board claims unless verified by tools or explicit game_state.

tools_schema.name: inspect_node
tools_schema.description: Get detailed information about a specific node on the board. USE THIS to verify node data instead of trying to interpret Arrays N and H yourself - this prevents hallucinations!

reasoning.description: Explain WHY you're inspecting this specific node. What are you trying to verify or learn?

tools_schema.name: inspect_hex
tools_schema.description: Get detailed information about a specific hex/tile on the board, including resource, number, pips, robber status, adjacent nodes, and adjacent buildings. USE THIS before robber moves instead of manually reverse-mapping Arrays N and H.

reasoning.description: Explain WHY you're inspecting this specific hex. What robber target or production claim are you verifying?

tools_schema.name: find_best_nodes
tools_schema.description: Search for the best available nodes matching specific criteria. USE THIS instead of manually scanning the board - prevents missing opportunities!

reasoning.description: Explain your search strategy. What kind of position are you looking for and why?

min_pips.description: Minimum total pip value (probability). Good nodes have 10+, excellent have 12+

exclude_blocked.description: Skip nodes that cannot be built on (occupied or too close to other buildings)

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return

tools_schema.name: analyze_path_potential
tools_schema.description: Analyze where a road path leads and what opportunities exist ahead. USE THIS to plan road building - shows ports and valuable nodes 1-2 steps away!

reasoning.description: Explain your road-building strategy. Why analyze this path? What are you hoping to reach?

from_node.description: Starting node ID (where you currently have a settlement/road)

direction_node.description: Specific neighbor to analyze, or omit to see all directions

max_depth.description: How many steps ahead to look (1 or 2)
